applicationInfo.name: Threat Model Export
applicationInfo.description: Educational security demonstration ("Dogwood Gateway" / "AgentCore Gateway + Dogwood"). A public AWS sample that shows temporal authorization policies (Dogwood language) and rate limiting enforced at Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway. A real LLM agent (Bedrock Converse tool-use loop) calls synthetic banking/trading tools through the gateway; every call crosses a policy engine that enforces session-aware Dogwood policies (output-to-input integrity, cumulative budget, one-time-use approvals) plus gateway rate limits. A React dashboard visualizes each tool call and the gateway's verdict. Intended to be deployed to a sandbox account, demonstrated, and torn down. All banking/trading data is synthetic and hardcoded; no real funds, customers, or PII exist. Not a production system.

mitigations.content: API Gateway JWT authorizer on every route (/config,/run,/events,/mode) validates a Cognito access token; unauthenticated requests are rejected before Lambda. Verified in the smoke test (401).
Cognito self sign-up disabled; the first operator is created by deploy.sh via admin-create-user; preventUserExistenceErrors enabled. Additional users only via admin action.
Dogwood policy TransferRequiresLookup (output-to-input integrity): transfer_funds permitted only when a prior get_account_balance response in-session returned the destination account.
Dogwood policy SessionBudgetCap (sum aggregation): forbids purchase_item once the session's cumulative amount exceeds the budget, including the current request.

Dogwood policies TradeRequiresUnusedApproval (negated-left since) and TradeOneAttemptPerApproval (anchored count + bind): a trade is permitted only while no completed trade has occurred since a matching approval for the exact ticker and quantity, and a forbid counts execution attempts (including in-flight requests) since the last matching approval, so concurrent double-execution against one approval is denied.
Policy engine runs ENFORCE, deny-by-default, at the gateway outside agent code; the agent cannot see or reason around the policies. Enforced on every tools/call.
Gateway rate limit (1 req/s on the failing tool, 300/min wildcard) plus per-invocation Lambda timeout and a hard tool-call budget in the agent bound runaway consumption.
Transport & storage hardening: private S3 with CloudFront Origin Access Control, enforceSSL, TLS everywhere, DynamoDB encryption at rest with 24h TTL, synthetic data only.
iam:PassRole for the gateway role is constrained with a PassedToService condition (bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com); gateway role invoke is scoped to the BankTools function ARN.
Scope the Agent Lambda's bedrock:InvokeModel to the configured model ARNs (specific inference profile + that model's foundation-model ARN) instead of foundation-model/* and inference-profile/*.
RECOMMENDED for production: enable AgentCore Gateway application logs (OTEL) and API Gateway access logs to attribute mode flips and runs; the demo relies on CloudTrail only.
ACCEPTED for demo / documented: gateway exceptionLevel is DEBUG so the dashboard can show denial reasons verbatim. In production use a less verbose level to avoid disclosing policy structure.

ACCEPTED for demo / documented: session-scoped temporal controls (budget, rate, approvals) shape behavior within a cooperative session; a caller controlling their own session id can reset counters. Not a hard boundary.
ACCEPTED for demo / documented: the LOG_ONLY toggle is an intentional teaching feature exposed through the authenticated API; it makes enforcement observe-only. Not present in a production posture.

RECOMMENDED / defense-in-depth: pin dependency versions and scan with CVE tooling; add SPDX/MIT-0 license headers; consider AWS WAF on CloudFront/API and cdk-nag suppressions with justifications for production.

Dogwood policy TaintedSessionNoTransfer (forbid + formerly): once a read_market_research response exists in the session, transfer_funds is forbidden for the rest of the session. A forbid overrides every permit, so prompt-injection containment holds even for transfers that satisfy TransferRequiresLookup, and regardless of whether the injection fooled the model. Demonstrated in Act 6.

threats.threatSource: An unauthenticated internet user who discovered the CloudFront/API URL
threats.prerequisites: network access to the public API endpoint, no valid token
threats.threatAction: call demo API routes (/run, /mode, /events) without a Cognito JWT
threats.threatImpact: unauthorized control of the demo and its Bedrock/gateway spend
threats.statement: A An unauthenticated internet user who discovered the CloudFront/API URL network access to the public API endpoint, no valid token can call demo API routes (/run, /mode, /events) without a Cognito JWT, which leads to unauthorized control of the demo and its Bedrock/gateway spend

threats.threatSource: An external actor with the public Cognito client id and hosted-UI URL
threats.prerequisites: knowledge of the user pool hosted UI (client id is public in config.json)
threats.threatAction: self-register a new account to obtain a valid JWT
threats.threatImpact: bypass of the intended allowlist of operators
threats.statement: A An external actor with the public Cognito client id and hosted-UI URL knowledge of the user pool hosted UI (client id is public in config.json) can self-register a new account to obtain a valid JWT, which leads to bypass of the intended allowlist of operators

threats.threatSource: A manipulated agent (prompt injection in a user message or tool output)
threats.prerequisites: attacker-controlled text reaches the model; agent holds valid gateway credentials
threats.threatAction: call transfer_funds with a fabricated destination account never returned by a lookup
threats.threatImpact: funds routed to an attacker account (in a real deployment)
threats.statement: A A manipulated agent (prompt injection in a user message or tool output) attacker-controlled text reaches the model; agent holds valid gateway credentials can call transfer_funds with a fabricated destination account never returned by a lookup, which leads to funds routed to an attacker account (in a real deployment)

threats.prerequisites: agent can issue many tool calls in a session
threats.threatAction: salami-slice many sub-threshold purchases to exceed the intended session budget
threats.threatImpact: cumulative financial exposure beyond what any single approval allowed
threats.statement: A A runaway or manipulated agent agent can issue many tool calls in a session can salami-slice many sub-threshold purchases to exceed the intended session budget, which leads to cumulative financial exposure beyond what any single approval allowed

threats.threatSource: A manipulated agent reusing a standing approval
threats.prerequisites: one approval event exists in the session trajectory
threats.threatAction: execute the same trade multiple times against a single one-time approval
threats.threatImpact: approval replay multiplies exposure a human signed off once
threats.statement: A A manipulated agent reusing a standing approval one approval event exists in the session trajectory can execute the same trade multiple times against a single one-time approval, which leads to approval replay multiplies exposure a human signed off once

threats.threatSource: A caller who controls their own policy-session id
threats.threatAction: start a fresh session to reset session-scoped counters (budget, rate, approvals)
threats.threatImpact: session-scoped temporal controls do not bound a determined caller
threats.statement: A A caller who controls their own policy-session id ability to set the x-amzn-bedrock-agentcore-policy-session-id header can start a fresh session to reset session-scoped counters (budget, rate, approvals), which leads to session-scoped temporal controls do not bound a determined caller

threats.threatAction: flip the policy engine to LOG_ONLY and leave it there
threats.threatImpact: all temporal enforcement silently becomes observe-only; denials stop
threats.statement: A Any operator with dashboard access valid Cognito JWT can flip the policy engine to LOG_ONLY and leave it there, which leads to all temporal enforcement silently becomes observe-only; denials stop

threats.threatSource: A runaway agent hitting a failing tool
threats.prerequisites: a tool that errors and an agent that retries
threats.threatAction: flood the gateway with tool calls, or drive heavy Bedrock token/connection use
threats.threatImpact: cost blow-up and starvation of other traffic
threats.statement: A A runaway agent hitting a failing tool a tool that errors and an agent that retries can flood the gateway with tool calls, or drive heavy Bedrock token/connection use, which leads to cost blow-up and starvation of other traffic

threats.threatSource: Cost/DoS via the direct inference path
threats.prerequisites: agent invokes Bedrock directly (not through the gateway)
threats.threatAction: consume Bedrock tokens in a long tool-use loop
threats.threatImpact: Bedrock spend not bounded by any gateway rate limit
threats.statement: A Cost/DoS via the direct inference path agent invokes Bedrock directly (not through the gateway) can consume Bedrock tokens in a long tool-use loop, which leads to Bedrock spend not bounded by any gateway rate limit

threats.threatSource: An attacker probing IAM blast radius
threats.prerequisites: compromise of the Agent Lambda execution role
threats.threatAction: invoke any Bedrock foundation model / inference profile via the broad InvokeModel grant
threats.threatImpact: wider model access and cost than the demo needs
threats.statement: A An attacker probing IAM blast radius compromise of the Agent Lambda execution role can invoke any Bedrock foundation model / inference profile via the broad InvokeModel grant, which leads to wider model access and cost than the demo needs

threats.threatSource: An attacker with a foothold in the browser (XSS)

threats.threatAction: read the JWT access token from sessionStorage
threats.threatImpact: token theft and demo-API impersonation until token expiry
threats.statement: A An attacker with a foothold in the browser (XSS) an XSS sink in the SPA (none obvious; React, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML) can read the JWT access token from sessionStorage, which leads to token theft and demo-API impersonation until token expiry
